subject: Post-call: prompt corpus + regression benchmark next steps
messages:
From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.inference>
To: Amit Shah <amit@veridian.ai>, Nora Patel <nora.patel@finlytics.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.inference>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.inference>
Date: 2026-10-19T14:05:00-07:00
Subject: Post-call: prompt corpus + regression benchmark next steps

Hi Amit / Nora — thanks again for the demo today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can prioritize the eval and POC: 

- Recap: Veridian is looking to add an LLM-driven assistant for developer docs search + summarization. Primary concerns: answer accuracy on technical Qs, hallucination / attribution, and PII handling.
- Recommended starting models (based on your latency & cost targets):
  * redwood-2-7b-q4 (fast, lower cost; good for retrieval + summarization when paired with prompt templates)
  * redwood-3-13b (higher accuracy for open-ended synthesis; reserve for A/B on high-value flows)
  * fallback: open-compat-immutable-16b (for rare long-form replies)
- Benchmarks: I’ve uploaded a short benchmark harness and baseline results to the folder below. Those are synthetic, we’ll re-run with your prompts.
  https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1abcDEFbenchmarks

Action items I propose from our side: 
1) Please share a representative prompt corpus (customer queries + edge cases) — we need ~200–500 examples across flows. If possible, include a label for acceptability (OK / risky) and highlight any examples with PII.
2) Highlight redaction requirements (fields to remove/mask) and any company-specific sensitive tokens.
3) Tell us your regression tolerance (e.g., top-1 accuracy drop allowed, or a conversational F1 threshold). If you don’t have one, we’ll propose a baseline and show tradeoffs.
4) Schedule a short (60m) technical workshop with your data team to review prompt formatting and redaction — are you available next Tue/Wed?

Attachments I can accept: CSV or JSONL prompt dumps, a short doc with redaction rules, and any sample expected outputs.

I’m copying Ben to coordinate commercial/POC steps and Irene for SOC2/compliance items.

Thanks — looking forward to the samples so we can run the reg test and recommend quantization/latency knobs.

—
Logan Wright
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
logan.wright@redwood.inference | +1 (415) 555-0198

From: Amit Shah <amit@veridian.ai>

Date: 2026-10-19T17:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: prompt corpus + regression benchmark next steps

Thanks Logan — great summary. We have an initial set of ~120 prompts and a handful of flagged edge cases (mostly containing stack traces and config snippets). I’ve attached a CSV extract (veridian_prompt_samples.csv) for your ingestion. A few quick clarifications: 

- Redaction: we need masking for any API keys, long commit hashes, and full-stack traces longer than 3 lines. Inline IPs are ok to keep if anonymized (x.x.x.x -> 10.0.0.1-style).
- Labels: we don’t yet have a binary acceptability label across all rows; I can add a simple manual pass for ~50 critical prompts this week.
- Regression tolerance: we’d prefer <3% top-1 regression on our internal accuracy set for high-priority intents; for exploratory flows we can accept 5–8% in exchange for throughput.

Also — two asks: can Redwood provide a short script or instructions for converting CSV -> JSONL with metadata fields you expect? And, do you recommend we send full user+system prompt pairs or de-duplicated user queries only?

Attaching: veridian_prompt_samples.csv (partial)

1) POC timeline: we typically run a 4-week technical POC once we have prompt corpus + access (API key or dedicated staging). If you’re aiming for November pilot, we should lock scope this week.
2) Procurement: what’s your procurement cadence for a POC? If you need an MSA/SOW, I can route draft documents — otherwise we can run on a standard POC agreement.

Irene — can we get a short SOC2 evidence checklist to share with Amit (hosted vs private deployment options) so they can prep?

Hi all — attaching the full prompt dump (veridian_prompt_samples.csv) and a short doc with our redaction guidance (veridian_poc_policy.pdf). A few specifics from our side: 

- Prompt composition: send both user+system pairs where available. The system role often contains routing hints we use downstream. If you accept CSV, include columns: id, user_prompt, system_prompt, expected_response (optional), priority.
- Edge cases: we’ve flagged ~20 examples with embedded commit hashes and customer account numbers — those should be treated as sensitive and redacted.
- Quantization question: we’d like guidance on 4-bit quantized models for latency savings. For code-like answers (stack traces + diffs) we prioritize correctness; is redwood-3-13b q4 a safe starting point?

Next steps: please confirm ingestion format and a time for the 60m technical workshop. I can do Thu 10/22 10:00–11:00PT or Fri 10/23 14:00–15:00PT.
